events.text: Irene Kharisma Sukandar was born in Jakarta.
events.subject: self
events.quote: born 7 April 1992 in Jakarta

events.text: Sukandar won the Indonesian Womens Chess Championship four times in a row starting in 2006.
events.subject: self
events.quote: won the Indonesian Womens Chess Championship four times in a row from 2006 to 2010

events.text: Sukandar's run of Indonesian Womens Chess Championship wins ended in 2010.
events.subject: self
events.quote: four times in a row from 2006 to 2010

events.text: Sukandar began representing Indonesia in Womens Chess Olympiads in 2004.
events.subject: self
events.quote: represented Indonesia in five Womens Chess Olympiads from 2004 to 2014

events.text: Sukandar's Womens Chess Olympiad representation ran through 2014.
events.subject: self
events.quote: five Womens Chess Olympiads from 2004 to 2014

events.text: Sukandar represented Indonesia at the Womens Asian Team Chess Championship in 2009.
events.subject: self
events.quote: the Womens Asian Team Chess Championship in 2009

events.text: Sukandar represented Indonesia at the World Youth Under-16 Chess Olympiad in 2007.
events.subject: self
events.quote: the World Youth Under-16 Chess Olympiad in 2007

events.text: Sukandar represented Indonesia at the 2006 Asian Games.
events.subject: self
events.quote: the 2006 Asian Games

events.text: Sukandar represented Indonesia at the 2009 Asian Indoor Games.
events.subject: self
events.quote: the 2009 Asian Indoor Games

events.text: Sukandar represented Indonesia at the 2013 Asian Indoor and Martial Arts Games.
events.subject: self
events.object: Asian Indoor and Martial Arts Games
events.quote: the 2013 Asian Indoor and Martial Arts Games

events.text: Sukandar won the individual silver medal on board 3 in the 36th Chess Olympiad in 2004.
events.subject: self
events.quote: won the individual silver medal on board 3 in the 36th Chess Olympiad in 2004

events.text: Sukandar was joint winner of the under-16 girls section of the 6th ASEAN Age Group Chess Championships in June 2005.
events.subject: self
events.quote: joint winner , with Vietnamese player Pham Bich Ngoc , of the under-16 girls section of the 6th ASEAN Age Group Chess Championships in Pattaya , Thailand in June 2005

events.text: Sukandar finished clear first in the under-18 girls division at the 2006 ASEAN Age Group Championships in Jakarta.
events.subject: self
events.quote: In the 2006 ASEAN Age Group Championships in Jakarta , she finished clear first in the under-18 girls division

events.text: In March 2008, Sukandar won the womens event of the 10th Rector Cup in Kharkiv, Ukraine.
events.subject: self
events.quote: In March 2008 , Sukandar won the womens event of the 10th Rector Cup in Kharkiv , Ukraine

events.text: In July 2010, Sukandar shared first place in the Brunei Invitational IM Tournament, earning an IM norm result.
events.subject: self
events.quote: In July 2010 , Sukandar shared first place with Indian FM Ramnath Bhuvanesh in the Brunei Invitational IM Tournament , earning an International Master ( IM ) norm result

events.text: Sukandar won the 2012 Asian Womens Chess Championship in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam.
events.subject: self
events.quote: She won the 2012 Asian Womens Chess Championship in Ho Chi Minh City , Vietnam

events.text: Sukandar qualified to play in the Womens World Championship 2014, which was postponed to 2015.
events.subject: self
events.quote: she qualified to play in the Womens World Championship 2014 , which was eventually postponed to 2015

events.text: In May 2013, Sukandar won the 5th Alexander The Great Open in Halkidiki, Greece.
events.subject: self
events.quote: In May 2013 , Sukandar won the 5th Alexander The Great Open , in Halkidiki , Greece

events.text: In December 2013, Sukandar won two individual gold medals for rapid and blitz chess at the 2013 Southeast Asian Games.
events.subject: self
events.quote: In December 2013 she won two individual gold medals , for rapid and blitz chess , at the 2013 Southeast Asian Games

events.text: In 2014, Sukandar won for the second time the Asian Womens Championship in Sharjah, United Arab Emirates.
events.subject: self
events.quote: In 2014 , Sukandar won for the second time the Asian Womens Championship

events.text: Sukandar's 2014 victory qualified her for the knockout Womens World Championship 2016.
events.subject: self
events.quote: This victory qualified her for the knockout Womens World Championship 2016

events.text: Sukandar won the G section of the 2015 Moscow Open with a score of 7.5/9.
events.subject: self
events.quote: She won the G section ( a ten-player round-robin tournament for female students ) of the 2015 Moscow Open with a score of 7.5/9

events.text: At the Womens World Chess Championship 2015, Sukandar was knocked out in the first round by Salome Melia.
events.subject: self
events.quote: At the Womens World Chess Championship 2015 , Sukandar was knocked out in the first round by Salome Melia

events.text: In 2016, Sukandar shared first place in the Master section of the Continental Class Championships in Herndon, Virginia.
events.subject: self
events.quote: In 2016 , she shared first place in the Master section of the Continental Class Championships in Herndon , Virginia

events.text: In 2016, Sukandar won the North Carolina Open with a score of 5/5 points.
events.subject: self
events.quote: won the North Carolina Open with a score of 5/5 points

events.text: In 2018, Sukandar was the best female player at the Doeberl Cup by scoring 5.5/9 points.
events.subject: self
events.quote: In 2018 , she was the best female player at the Doeberl Cup by scoring 5.5/9 points

events.text: In November 2018, Sukandar won the 2018 Hjorth Open by scoring 7.5/9 points.
events.subject: self
events.quote: In November 2018 , she won the 2018 Hjorth Open by scoring 7.5/9 points

events.text: Sukandar and Levy Rozman entered Indonesian news when Rozman was defeated by Dadang Subur.
events.subject: self
events.quote: entered Indonesian news in March 2021 when Rozman was defeated by an Indonesian chess player

events.text: Sukandar played against Subur in an over-the-board match set up and staked by Indonesian sponsors.
events.subject: self
events.quote: Sukandar played against Subur to prove his legitimacy

events.text: Subur was beaten with a score of 3–0.
events.subject: other
events.quote: Subur was beaten with a score of 3–0
